architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The measured local experiments establish thermal-hold instability as the failure mode, distinguish it from temperature-dependent viscosity level, and show large E2 realization spread. The paper-derived rheological rule is that process and realization state primarily shift viscosity scale while a transferable thermal-response shape can be used with a one-point in-range state anchor, but that rule is demonstrated only within the original local chemistry family. Curated PUR literature supports an acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier-like formulation family and broad regions, not an exact local property prediction or optimum. The conservative design constraint for performance mitigation requires retaining both independently supported intervention axes; minimum modifier burden can be used only among otherwise sufficient candidates. The Skeptic objection is decisive that S1C41's 15 wt% acrylic level is only directionally supported, that matched control and numerical acceptance rules are missing, and that modifier functionality may change stoichiometry. The Robustness Adjudicator likewise found process-state and stoichiometric interpretability failures and conditionally preferred S1C51 only if the 15 wt% acrylic evidence is discounted. Therefore no formulation is frozen as the performance result yet. The uncertainty probe must first verify modifier specifications and recalculated stoichiometry, add a contemporaneous identically processed E2/reactive-core control, freeze replication/blocking and numerical acceptance limits, and record complete process history. After those conditions are satisfied, S1C41 remains the lower-burden full-coverage candidate, while S1C51 is the conservative alternative if directly commensurate acrylic-region evidence is required.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: This is the required upstream bridge. It will establish the formulation-only versus state-aware model result, state-shift master-curve structure, one-point calibration value, local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, E1/E5 drift contrast, and the measurement rules needed before candidate comparison.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective and failure mode are established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, the original E2 reactive-core anchor, the independent acrylic and tackifier axes, and the historical/claim boundary before comparing any candidate formulations.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability at 120 C, including SI from 15 to 60 min and 15 to 90 min
Viscosity level at an anchor temperature within the measured 80 to 130 C support
Temperature-response behavior across the supported sweep, preferably using the state-aware temperature-sensitivity representation
Repeatability and realization spread across independent runs
Sensitivity to process history and whether one-point state calibration is required
Stoichiometric and process feasibility relative to the E2 reactive-core anchor
Acrylic-like modifier fraction and identity as a bounded intervention axis
Minor tackifier-like modifier fraction and identity as a separate bounded intervention axis
Extrapolation distance from locally measured composition and state
Evidence quality: directly commensurate numeric anchor versus directional or noncommensurate analogue evidence
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if evaluated at a state-calibrated viscosity rather than at nominal formulation identity alone?
Does the candidate reduce SI relative to the high-drift E5 reference without merely shifting the viscosity to an impractically low or high level?
Is the apparent benefit larger than the descriptive repeatability spread observed for E2?

Does adding the acrylic-like axis provide value beyond the minor tackifier-like axis, and does the combined intervention outperform each axis considered separately without exceeding bounded evidence-supported regions?
Would the decision change if external analogue percentages were treated only as directional priors rather than exact target levels?
Can the observed improvement be explained by a process-state or stoichiometric change rather than by the modifier intervention itself?
Does the candidate remain supported across the measured temperature sweep and the full 15 to 90 min hold window rather than only at a nominal endpoint?
planner.decision_goal: Select one bounded, evidence-supported formulation experiment intended to reduce thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving processable viscosity over the measured temperature range, without treating an external analogue level as an exact optimum.
design_implications: Rank candidates primarily by reduction of thermal-hold drift, not by nominal viscosity alone.
Evaluate viscosity level, temperature response, hold stability, repeatability, and process-state sensitivity as separate dimensions.
Use the original E2 reactive-core formulation as the local anchor while allowing independently supported acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes.

A combined modifier intervention is admissible for performance mitigation when each axis remains within bounded evidence-supported regions; single-axis isolation is not required because causal attribution is not the stated intent.
Keep acrylic loading and tackifier loading as explicit composition variables and preserve stoichiometric, process-history, and realization uncertainty rather than silently imputing them.
Use measured temperatures and the measured 15 to 90 min hold window for adjudication; do not convert longer-term external stability percentages into local thresholds.
Do not infer a molecular mechanism from the rheology; assess only whether the candidate reduces drift and remains feasible.
material_regularities_to_use: Temperature sweeps for E1, E2, and E3 are monotonically decreasing from 80 to 130 C, so viscosity level has a strong thermal response and must not be conflated with hold stability.

E2 has large descriptive nominal run spread across the measured temperature range, with sample CV approximately 0.46 to 0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios approximately 2.8 to 3.6; one nominal viscosity is therefore not sufficient to define the material response.
The original thermal-hold comparison shows a distinct stability contrast between E1 and E5 over the 15 to 90 min window at 120 C.
The measured temperature support is 80 to 130 C; candidate evaluation should remain inside this range unless an explicit extrapolation decision is made.
The state-shift and state-aware model findings must determine whether process-state calibration is needed before comparing candidate viscosity levels.

External acrylic and tackifier evidence supports formulation-family and direction hypotheses only; the supplied analogues are not directly commensurate exact local optima and generally lack the local hold protocol.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is the established failure mode: E5 shows large viscosity growth at 120 C from 15 to 60 min (SI=0.515) and 15 to 90 min (SI=0.931), compared with much smaller E1 drift (SI=0.095 and 0.168). This must be distinguished from temperature-dependent viscosity level and from substantial realization/process-state spread in E2.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep from 80 to 130 C, including viscosity at a predeclared anchor temperature within that range
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C at 15, 60, and 90 min, or the existing four-point schedule covering those endpoints
At least sufficient repeated runs to quantify descriptive run spread and distinguish candidate response from realization noise
Recorded preparation, mixing, drying, storage, and thermal-history details for process-state linkage
Confirmed formulation mass fractions and stoichiometric accounting, including reactive-core and modifier fractions
State-calibration measurement if the state-aware summary indicates that a one-point calibration materially improves comparability
Adjudication metrics for viscosity level, temperature response, hold SI, repeatability, and feasibility using frozen pre-result criteria
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary shows a large state shift or materially better state-aware than formulation-only prediction.
Candidate viscosity differences are smaller than the observed E2 run spread.
A candidate lies outside the 80 to 130 C temperature support or outside locally represented composition/state regions.
Acrylic or tackifier evidence is only directional or comes from noncommensurate chemistry, units, process history, or hold duration.
Modifier addition changes stoichiometry, reactive-group balance, or processing conditions in a way not represented by the local anchor.
Hold trajectories are nonmonotonic, incomplete, or confounded by temperature equilibration.
The candidate's apparent improvement occurs only at one nominal viscosity point and is not supported by hold or repeatability measurements.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates the local thermal-hold instability without relying on a static-viscosity shift or an uncontrolled realization-state change.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Accept as a provisional performance success only if the matched 120 C SI15-90 is materially below the E5 reference value of 0.931, the SI15-60 is materially below 0.515, the improvement is reproducible across independent runs beyond descriptive realization spread, and the 80-130 C response remains processable after state calibration. A stronger benchmark is approaching or remaining below the E1 SI values of 0.168 for 15-90 min and 0.095 for 15-60 min, but these are comparative local references rather than guaranteed thresholds.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the mitigation claim if drift is not reduced relative to E5, if apparent improvement occurs only at one nominal viscosity point, if candidate differences remain within realization noise, if hold data are incomplete or confounded by temperature equilibration, or if processability and state-calibrated temperature response are unacceptable.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min, plus the 80-130 C temperature sweep.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: State-calibrated thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 C, reported as SI from 15 to 60 min and from 15 to 90 min, with viscosity level, temperature response, repeatability, and process-state sensitivity reported separately.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 shows SI=0.515 from 15-60 min and SI=0.931 from 15-90 min at 120 C, versus E1 SI=0.095 and 0.168, establishing formulation-dependent thermal-hold instability.
Measured local evidence: E1, E2, and E3 temperature sweeps decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C, so viscosity level and temperature response must be separated from hold stability.
Measured local evidence: E2 has substantial realization spread, with approximate sample CV 0.46-0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios 2.8-3.6; one nominal viscosity measurement is insufficient.

Derived model rule: process and realization state primarily shift viscosity scale while a common thermal-response shape remains transferable; state-aware shared-shape fit is substantially better than formulation-only prediction.
Derived measurement rule: use one in-range state-specific viscosity anchor, preferably at 120 C, before comparing viscosity levels across realizations.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like PUR examples support a broad 15-25 wt% region; approximately 19-20 wt% examples are directly commensurate numeric anchors, while 15 wt% is directional/noncommensurate and 25 wt% has comparative stability evidence in different chemistry.
External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like PUR examples cluster near 4.8-6.4 wt%, with broader guidance below about 10 wt%; these are formulation-family priors, not local optima.
Conservative design principle: for performance_mitigation, both independently supported intervention axes must be covered before minimum total modifier burden is used as a tie-break.

Unresolved uncertainty: modifier identity, reactive-group functionality, process history, and state realization may affect hold stability independently of nominal composition; no molecular mechanism is inferred.
proposer.scientific_target: Reduce the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity drift of the E5-like failure mode while preserving processable viscosity and transferable temperature response across 80-130 C; test a full intervention covering both independently supported acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes rather than optimizing static viscosity alone.
unresolved_questions: Does the combined acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like intervention reduce SI beyond the observed E2 realization spread?
Is S1C41's lower-burden full-coverage formulation sufficient, or is the higher acrylic level in S1C46 needed?
Does acrylic-like modifier functionality or effective reactive-group density alter hold stability independently of loading?
Are candidate modifier fractions truly nonreactive or must the E2 stoichiometric accounting be recalculated?
How much of any observed improvement is formulation-driven versus process-state or realization-state driven?
Will the candidate remain stable across the full 80-130 C sweep and 15-90 min hold rather than only at 120 C?
The evidence supports a formulation region and family, not an exact optimum; exact literature-percentage distance should remain audit metadata rather than the optimization objective.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Retains full coverage and 5 wt% tackifier support at 22.5 wt% total burden, but 17.5 wt% remains an interpolated rather than directly commensurate acrylic anchor.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A compromise is desired between S1C41's minimum burden and the stronger approximately 20 wt% acrylic evidence region.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner single-axis attribution, but it does not satisfy the current performance-mitigation requirement for full independently supported axis coverage.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The immediate objective changes to causal isolation of the minor tackifier-like axis.

required_conditions: Add a contemporaneously prepared, identically processed E2 or reactive-core control, preferably in paired or blocked runs with the candidate.
Verify modifier identity, reactive-group functionality, equivalent weight, formulation denominator, and recalculate NCO:OH stoichiometry before testing.
Predeclare independent preparation count, technical replicate structure, randomization or blocking, and a quantitative rule for improvement beyond E2 realization spread.
Freeze numerical limits for SI15-60, SI15-90, processable viscosity, temperature response, and allowable state-calibration error.
Record complete preparation, mixing, drying, storage, sample-age, and thermal-history metadata and flag uncontrolled state differences.
If retaining S1C41, describe 15 wt% acrylic as a directional design point rather than a directly commensurate optimum; otherwise use S1C51 as the conservative full-coverage probe.
Do not interpret a candidate result as a mitigation success without complete 120 C hold data, the 80-130 C sweep, state calibration, and matched-control comparison.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 directly tests the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure using SI15-60 and SI15-90, while separating drift from static viscosity and temperature response.
The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis intervention is scientifically appropriate; causal isolation is not the stated objective.
S1C41 covers both independently supported axes, acrylic_like and minor_tackifier_like. Its full coverage is preferable to partial-coverage candidates for the primary mitigation test.

S1C41 has the lowest burden among the proposed clearly supported full-coverage candidates, but its 15 wt% acrylic level relies mainly on directional, noncommensurate evidence. It must not be promoted solely on burden if that evidence is discounted.
Treating evidence as supported regions leaves S1C41 admissible, but a conservative interpretation excluding the 15 wt% acrylic point favors a 20 wt% acrylic full-coverage candidate such as S1C51.

Six process-history fields are missing, E2 realization spread is large, and no contemporaneous matched E2 or reactive-core control is explicitly required. A state anchor alone cannot distinguish formulation benefit from state or batch effects.

The proposed 120 C hold, 80-130 C sweep, and state calibration address the intended claim, but replication, blocking or randomization, numerical processability limits, effect-size thresholds, and a matched control must be frozen.
Modifier identity, equivalent weight, reactive-group functionality, and denominator are unresolved; the original E2 NCO:OH ratio cannot be assumed valid after both modifiers are added.
The recommendation depends on treating 15 wt% acrylic as sufficiently supported and on extrapolating the local state-aware shared-shape model to a dual-modifier chemistry.

The Skeptic identified high-severity interpretability and acceptance-criterion problems. These warrant an uncertainty probe or conditional reranking before accepting S1C41 as the primary performance point.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not show that S1C41 would remain preferred if the 15 wt% acrylic evidence were treated only as directional and the directly commensurate approximately 19-20 wt% acrylic region were prioritized.
The proposal does not establish that S1C41's lower burden has comparable evidence coverage and interpretability to S1C46 once the noncommensurate 15 wt% acrylic denominator is discounted.
A null or small effect for S1C41 would be difficult to interpret as insufficient intervention versus absence of mitigation because no matched lower- or zero-modifier control is explicitly required.
The plan does not test whether the combined intervention adds value beyond each axis separately, despite listing that as a counterfactual question; the ranked experiment alone cannot answer it.
The proposal correctly avoids treating static viscosity as stability, but it does not predefine how a candidate with improved SI yet unacceptable state-calibrated viscosity will be adjudicated.

critical_findings.evidence: E2 shows substantial realization spread (CV approximately 0.46-0.58; maximum/minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6), while all candidates have six missing process-history fields. Existing E1/E5 references do not substitute for a matched control prepared and measured under the same process history.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed experiment lacks an explicitly matched contemporaneous E2 or other local control, making it difficult to distinguish candidate benefit from batch, process-state, and realization effects.

critical_findings.evidence: The proposer uses 'materially below,' 'reproducible across independent runs beyond descriptive realization spread,' and 'processable' without numerical effect-size, replication, uncertainty, or processability limits. The E1 values are explicitly described as comparative references rather than thresholds.
critical_findings.issue: Acceptance criteria are not operationally frozen enough for adjudication.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 replaces 20 wt% of the formulation with acrylic-like and tackifier-like material while retaining nominal E2 core proportions. The payload states that reactive-group functionality may require recalculation of the original NCO:OH 1.80 ratio, but modifier identity and functionality are unspecified.
critical_findings.issue: Stoichiometric and process-state confounding remains unresolved for the selected combined formulation.

critical_findings.evidence: The 15 wt% acrylic evidence is explicitly labeled provisional and noncommensurate, with its fraction denominator requiring reverification. Directly commensurate acrylic anchors cluster near 19.37-19.98 wt% and 25 wt%, whereas S1C41 uses 15 wt%.
critical_findings.issue: The acrylic loading is treated as a sufficiently supported total-formulation anchor more strongly than the evidence permits.

critical_findings.evidence: The statement that S1C41 is the 'smallest clearly evidence-supported combined intervention' depends on a conservative design rule and the exclusion of S1C40 because its 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. This is a defensible policy choice, not a directly measured literature fact or local optimum.
critical_findings.issue: The argument for minimum sufficient intervention is partly reconstructed rather than directly measured.

critical_findings.evidence: The state-aware model supports approximately 6-10% pooled multiplicative anchor error within the original local chemistry family, while S1C41 introduces external modifier chemistries. The model does not establish that the same shared thermal-response shape or state mapping remains valid after both modifiers are added.
critical_findings.issue: The state-anchor plan improves comparability of viscosity level but does not by itself establish thermal-hold stability equivalence or remove process-history confounding.

critical_findings.evidence: The 2.5 wt% acrylic difference is not an independently isolated factor in the ranked performance candidates, so a difference between S1C41 and S1C46 would not cleanly identify an acrylic-loading effect.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed rank ordering may overstate the interpretive value of comparing S1C41 with S1C46.

interpretability_failures: No explicitly specified matched E2/process control is included in the provisional measurement plan.
Replication count, randomization or blocking, and a quantitative definition of improvement beyond realization spread are unspecified.
Processability and acceptable viscosity-level limits are not numerically predeclared.
Modifier reactive-group identity, equivalent weight, and stoichiometric treatment are not fixed before interpretation.
A state anchor at 120 C cannot by itself separate modifier-driven stability changes from altered realization state or chemistry-family extrapolation.

leakage_check.detail: The payload states that validation formulation identity and outcome were excluded, and the tool reports validation_formulation_visible=false. However, it also states that the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. The supplied record therefore supports outcome-blind intent but cannot independently verify that the exact candidate construction and ranking were free of post-result operational influence.

regularity_alignment.detail: S1C41 correctly addresses the established 120 C thermal-hold drift, provides full coverage of both independently supported intervention axes, separates hold stability from static viscosity, and includes state calibration. However, its 15 wt% acrylic level is supported primarily by directional/noncommensurate evidence, and the claim that it is the smallest clearly evidence-supported full-coverage intervention is not fully secure.

required_corrections: Add a contemporaneously prepared and identically processed E2 or reactive-core control, preferably with paired or blocked runs against S1C41.
Predeclare the number of independent preparations and technical measurements, randomization or blocking, and the statistical or descriptive rule for exceeding realization spread.
Freeze numerical acceptance limits for SI15-60, SI15-90, processable viscosity range, temperature-response behavior, and allowable state-calibration error before testing.
Verify modifier composition, equivalent weight, reactive-group functionality, and total-formulation denominator; recalculate NCO:OH stoichiometry before ranking the result.
Record complete preparation, mixing, drying, storage, sample-age, and thermal-history metadata and reject or flag runs with uncontrolled state differences.
Describe S1C41's 15 wt% acrylic level explicitly as a conservative directional design point, not a directly commensurate optimum or exact literature anchor.
Retain S1C41 as the provisional full-coverage candidate only after these controls are added; do not present it as proven minimum sufficient intervention before intervention sufficiency is measured.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundaries: it does not infer a molecular mechanism, does not use analogue percentages as exact optima, and directly measures the local hold failure. The remaining boundary concern is extrapolation of the local state-aware shared-shape model from the original chemistry family to a dual-modifier formulation with unresolved functionality and process history.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This is the required upstream bridge. It will establish the formulation-only versus state-aware model result, state-shift master-curve structure, one-point calibration value, local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, E1/E5 drift contrast, and the measurement rules needed before candidate comparison.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
